subject.title: Telegram message(action=send) can prematurely release Codex turn in message_tool_only mode

question: Should message-tool-only turns distinguish progress sends from final source replies, or should every `message(action=send)` remain a terminal turn-control action?
rationale: The shipped terminal behavior prevents stuck final replies, while the reported workflow requires visible intermediate sends to continue the same turn; source inspection cannot choose which public message-result contract maintainers intend.

options.title: Add typed progress disposition
options.body: Introduce a shared progress-versus-final result contract and release Codex turns only for explicitly final source replies.

options.title: Keep message sends terminal
options.body: Preserve the current contract and route progress through a separate commentary, streaming, or channel-progress surface instead of `message(action=send)`.

options.title: Remove terminal release
options.body: Treat all message sends as ordinary non-terminal tools and rely on `turn/completed` plus the existing watchdog, accepting possible regression of the previously stuck final-reply case.

recommendation.title: Add typed progress disposition
recommendation.body: Introduce a shared progress-versus-final result contract and release Codex turns only for explicitly final source replies.

likelyOwner.reason: The most directly related shipped behavior is the v2026.7.1 message-tool-only Codex completion fix credited to this person.
